{{George Best series}}
'''George Best''' (22 May 1946 – 25 November 2005) was a Northern Irish professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[right winger (association football)|right winger]], spending most of his club career at [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]. A skillful [[Dribbling|dribbler]], he is considered one of the greatest players of all time,<ref name="May">{{cite news|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/4309502.stm|title=Was Georgie the Best?|date=25 November 2005|work=BBC Sport|access-date=12 October 2018|archive-date=25 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160625195651/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/4309502.stm|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-18 |title=The 50 Greatest Soccer Players of All Time |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/the-50-greatest-soccer-players-of-all-time |access-date=2025-09-17 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en-US}}</ref> along with being considered one of the most talented to play.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |last=Safin |first=Muhammed Maklet |date=18 March 2009 |title=Seven Most Naturally Gifted Footballers Ever |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/140983-seven-most-naturally-gifted-footballers-ever |access-date=23 November 2023 |website=Bleacher Report }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Football |first=Planet |date=22 May 2023 |title=13 of the best quotes on George Best: 'It was paradise watching him play' |url=https://www.planetfootball.com/quick-reads/11-of-the-best-quotes-on-george-best-it-was-paradise-watching-him-play-football |access-date=23 November 2023 |website=Planet Football }}</ref> He was named [[European Footballer of the Year]] in 1968 and came fifth in the [[FIFA Player of the Century#FIFA Magazine and Grand Jury vote|FIFA Player of the Century]] vote. Best received plaudits for his playing style, which combined pace, skill, balance, [[Dummy (football)|feints]], the ability to get past defenders and goalscoring. In 1999 he was on the six-man shortlist for the BBC's [[BBC Sports Personality of the Year#Sports Personality of the Century Award|Sports Personality of the Century]]. He was an inaugural inductee into the [[English Football Hall of Fame]] in 2002.

Born in [[Belfast]], Best began his club career in England with Manchester United, with the scout who had spotted his talent at the age of 15 sending a telegram to manager [[Matt Busby]] which read: "I think I've found you a genius". After making his debut at age 17, he scored 179 goals in 470 appearances over 11 years and was the club's [[List of Manchester United F.C. seasons#Seasons|top goalscorer]] in the league for five consecutive seasons.<ref>''Reliving the Dream: The Triumph and Tears of Manchester United's 1968 European Cup Heroes''. Random House,</ref> He won two [[List of English football champions#Total titles won|League titles]], two [[FA Community Shield|Charity Shield]]s and the [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]] with the club.

In international football, Best was [[Cap (sport)|capped]] 37 times for [[Northern Ireland national football team|Northern Ireland]] between 1964 and 1977. A combination of the team's performance and his lack of fitness in 1982 meant that he never played in the finals of a major tournament. He considered his international career as being "recreational football", with the expectations placed on a smaller nation in Northern Ireland being much less than with his club. He is regarded as one of the greatest players never to have played at a [[FIFA World Cup|World Cup]]. The [[Irish Football Association]] described him as the "greatest player to ever pull on the green shirt of Northern Ireland".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irishfa.com/international/squad-profiles/profile/341/legends-of-the-game/george-best|title=George Best|date=1 November 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121101012945/http://www.irishfa.com/international/squad-profiles/profile/341/legends-of-the-game/george-best |archive-date=1 November 2012 }}</ref>

With his good looks, dark [[The Beatles|Beatle]] mop-top hair and [[playboy lifestyle]], Best became one of the first media celebrity footballers, earning the nickname "[[Fifth Beatle|o Quinto Beatle]]" by Portuguese press reporters after a stand-out performance for Manchester United in Lisbon in March 1966. However, his extravagant lifestyle led to various personal problems, most notably [[alcoholism]], from which he suffered for the rest of his life. These issues affected him on and off the field, often causing controversy.<ref name=LongGoodbye>Gordon Burn, [https://www.theguardian.com/g2/story/0,3604,1650397,00.html "The Long Goodbye"], ''[[The Guardian]]'' (London), 25 November 2005</ref> Although conscious of his problems, he made light of them and was known for his intelligence and wit on the subject during periods of sobriety: "I spent a lot of money on booze, girls and fast cars – the rest I just squandered".<ref>{{cite news |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/4090840.stm |work=[[BBC News]] |title=Best: Decline of the golden boy |date=14 June 2005 |access-date=14 August 2013 |archive-date=14 May 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140514163912/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/4090840.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> After football, he spent some time as a [[Pundit|football analyst]], but his financial and health problems continued into his retirement. He died in 2005, aged 59, from complications from the [[immunosuppressive drug]]s he needed to take after a [[Liver transplantation|liver transplant]] in 2002.

== Early years and family ==
[[File:Burren Way, Cregagh Estate - geograph.org.uk - 1392932.jpg|thumb|right|Best grew up on the [[Cregagh]] estate, east [[Belfast]]. The playing fields in the estate where he played football as a boy, Cregagh Green, is protected for community recreation in perpetuity as a [[Fields in Trust]] Active Space.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fieldsintrust.org/ArchivedNews/active-spaces--belfast%E2%80%99s-cregagh-green-first-to-benefit-from-london-marathon-charitable-trust|title=ACTIVE SPACES: Belfast's Cregagh Green first to benefit from London Marathon Charitable Trust funding |publisher=Fields in Trust |access-date=13 October 2020|archive-date=12 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200812210109/http://fieldsintrust.org/ArchivedNews/active-spaces--belfast%E2%80%99s-cregagh-green-first-to-benefit-from-london-marathon-charitable-trust |url-status=live}}</ref>]] George Best was born on 22 May 1946 in [[Belfast]], the first child of Richard "Dickie" Best (1919–2008) and Anne Withers (1922–1978). He was raised in the [[Cregagh]] estate in east Belfast. Best had five siblings: four sisters, Carol, Barbara, Julie, and Grace, and one brother, Ian Busby Best.<ref>{{cite news |title=Family, friends and team-mates: they were there with George until the very end |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/news-and-comment/family-friends-and-team-mates-they-were-there-with-george-until-the-very-end-516982.html |access-date=10 October 2020 |newspaper=The Independent |archive-date=4 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221004160605/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/news/family-friends-and-teammates-they-were-there-with-george-until-the-very-end-516982.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Best's mother, herself an Irish hockey international, recalled that the boy was able to stand aged ten months and from then on was never seen without a ball at his feet, even taking one to bed.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/iplayer/episodes/b08s3wxj/george-best-all-by-himself 'George Best: All by Himself']. BBC, 2017. Retrieved 26 November 2025</ref> His father was a member of the [[Orange Order]] and as a boy George carried the strings of the banner in his local Cregagh lodge. In his autobiography, Best mentioned how important the Order was to his family.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.goli.org.uk/ |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100925205154/http://www.grandorangelodge.co.uk/press/PressReleases-2009/090709-goerge_best_collarette_in_exhibition.htm|url-status=dead|title=Grand Orange Lodge of Ireland &#124; Fraternal Organisation &#124; Belfast |archive-date=25 September 2010 |website=GOLI}}</ref> The Best family was raised in the [[Free Presbyterian Church of Ulster|Free Presbyterian]] faith.<ref name=Andrews>{{cite book|last=Andrews|first=David L |title=Manchester United: a thematic study|year=2004|publisher=Routledge|location=Abingdon, Oxfordshire|isbn=0-415-33333-4 |page=135 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ueYTmo5apM4C&pg=PA135 }}</ref>

In 1957, the academically gifted Best passed the [[Eleven-plus|11-plus]] and went to [[Grosvenor Grammar School|Grosvenor High School]], but he soon played truant as the school specialised in [[rugby union]]. Best then moved to Lisnasharragh Secondary School, reuniting him with friends from primary school and allowing him to focus on football. He played for [[Cregagh Boys Club]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Your Place And Mine - George Best 1946 - 2005 |publisher=BBC Northern Ireland |access-date=13 January 2019 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/northernireland/yourplaceandmine/archive/A877188.shtml |archive-date=30 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220130175238/https://www.bbc.co.uk/northernireland/yourplaceandmine/archive/A877188.shtml |url-status=live }}</ref> He grew up supporting [[Glentoran F.C.|Glentoran]] and [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]].<ref>{{harvnb|Best|2005|p=4}}</ref>

Anne Best died from alcoholism-related [[cardiovascular disease]] in 1978, at the age of 55.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/opinion/george-best-drama-an-intrusive-film-that-failed-to-tell-the-whole-story-14282152.html |title=George Best drama: an intrusive film that failed to tell the whole story |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20101015121418/http://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/opinion/george-best-drama-an-intrusive-film-that-failed-to-tell-the-whole-story-14282152.html |archivedate=15 October 2010 |work=Belfast Telegraph |accessdate=10 October 2020 }}</ref> Best's father died on 16 April 2008, 3 years after George's death, at the age of 88, in the [[Ulster Hospital]] in [[Dundonald, County Down|Dundonald]], Northern Ireland.<ref>{{cite news |title=George Best's dad dies of a broken heart grieving for son |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/3am/celebrity-news/george-bests-dad-dies-of-a-broken-303227 |work=Mirror.co.uk |date=17 April 2008 |accessdate=11 March 2022 |archive-date=24 April 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160424210557/http://www.mirror.co.uk/3am/celebrity-news/george-bests-dad-dies-of-a-broken-303227 |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Club career ==
=== Manchester United ===
At the age of 15, Best was discovered in [[Belfast]] by [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] scout Bob Bishop, whose telegram to United manager [[Matt Busby]] read: "I think I've found you a genius."<ref>{{cite news |first=Stephen |last=McGinty |url=http://news.scotsman.com/topics.cfm?tid=505&id=2300312005 |title=Best coming to the end of his life |work=[[The Scotsman]] |date=25 November 2005 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070210154147/http://news.scotsman.com/topics.cfm?tid=505 |archivedate=10 February 2007 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.talkfootball.co.uk/guides/football_legends_george_best.html |title=George Best |access-date=5 March 2008 |publisher=Talk Football |archive-date=25 February 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080225142744/http://www.talkfootball.co.uk/guides/football_legends_george_best.html |url-status=live }}</ref> His local club [[Glentoran F.C.|Glentoran]] had previously rejected him for being "too small and light".<ref>{{cite news |first=Anne |last=Cadwallader |url=http://www.tiscali.co.uk/news/newswire.php/news/reuters/2005/11/25/sport/besttoosmallandlightforlocalclubasteen.html |title=Best too small and light for local club as teen |work=Tiscali News |date=25 November 2005 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070213081438/http://www.tiscali.co.uk/news/newswire.php/news/reuters/2005/11/25/sport/besttoosmallandlightforlocalclubasteen.html |archivedate=13 February 2007 }}</ref> Best was subsequently given a trial and signed up by United's chief scout [[Joe Armstrong (football scout)|Joe Armstrong]]. His first time moving to the club, Best quickly became homesick and stayed for only two days before going back home to Northern Ireland.<ref name="George Best">{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pLbPmolooK8 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111125092934/http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pLbPmolooK8&gl=US&hl=en| archive-date=25 November 2011 | url-status=dead|title=George Best Interview from 1972 |publisher=Barnjournalen |year=1972 |access-date=10 February 2008}}</ref> He returned to Manchester and spent two years as an amateur, as English clubs were not allowed to take Northern Irish players on as apprentices. He was given a job as an errand boy on the [[Manchester Ship Canal]], allowing him to train with the club twice a week.<ref>{{harvnb|Best|2005|p=3}}</ref>

Best made his [[Football League First Division|First Division]] debut, aged 17, on 14 September 1963 against [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] at [[Old Trafford]] in a 1–0 victory.<ref name="page 1">{{harvnb|Best|2005|p=1}}</ref> He then dropped back into the [[Manchester United F.C. Reserves and Academy|reserves]], before scoring his first goal for the first team in his second appearance in a 5–1 win over [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] on 28 December.<ref name="page 1"/> Manager [[Matt Busby]] then kept Best in the team; by the end of the [[1963–64 Manchester United F.C. season|1963–64]] season, he had made 26 appearances, scoring six goals. Manchester United finished second, four points behind [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]].<ref name="auto">{{harvnb|Best|2005|p=34}}</ref>

They reached the [[FA Cup semi-finals|semi-finals]] of the [[FA Cup]], where a defeat to [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] cost Best the chance to break a record. In [[1964 FA Cup Final|the final]] [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]]'s [[Howard Kendall]] became the youngest ever player in a [[FA Cup Final]] – he shared the same birth date as Best.<ref name="auto"/> That same season, Best captained the [[Manchester United F.C. Reserves and Academy|Manchester United]] side that won the 1964 [[FA Youth Cup]], the sixth FA Youth Cup won under the management of [[Jimmy Murphy (footballer)|Jimmy Murphy]] and the first since the 1958 [[Munich air disaster]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Ponting |first1=Ivan |title=George Best |date=2012 |publisher=Simon and Schuster |page=85}}</ref>
